messages:
alex: Heads-up — we have an active customer escalation from Acme Corp: multiple 5xx/timeouts hitting hosted inference endpoints since 08:12 UTC. Customer reports intermittent 502/504 and occasional 500 with long tail latency. Logs show many requests being admitted, then stuck in the continuous-batcher queue until they timeout.

maya: seeing same in prometheus. p95 token-latency up ~8x for that model, p99 even worse. Queue depth metric (request_queue_depth) spiked to 96/100 at 08:14. There were early-rejects disabled on that pool.

devon: error payload from gateway: `{"error":"upstream_timeout","detail":"request dropped after queue wait > 60s"}` — but some responses are 502 from nginx in front.

jess: customer sample curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-xl-1","input":"long document...","max_tokens":2000}'` returns 504 after ~62s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noticed a config change at 07:59 — continuous_batching.max_pending increased from 64 -> 100 for hosted-prod pool A.

alex: suspects the increased max_pending + several long-running seq-length=2048 requests caused headroom exhaustion. When batchers are full, dequeue stall -> backlog.

maya: quick triage: can we limit ingress to that pool? set `max_pending=40` and re-enable early_reject. If we can't change immediately, can route traffic to fallback model variant?

devon: trying an emergency config rollback to `max_pending=48` on pool A now. Rolling update id `roll-2026-03-15-09-03`

ingress-bot: routing rule updated: traffic for tenant=acme -> fallback-model rwd-std-1 (lower seq and faster) (applied).

jess: customer confirmed a drop in 5xx after 09:06; still seeing occasional 504s at 09:12.

maya: logs show KV-cache hit-rate unchanged. The issue is backlog at KVCACHE-aware batcher dequeue: `batcher_dequeue_latency_ms` jumped from 10ms -> 12000ms for some workers.

devon: reproduced locally with synthetic load: mix of long-seq requests (seq=1700 tokens) + concurrent small requests. Continuous batching produced giant batches and hold times soared.

alex: reproduction steps we used:
1) `ab -n 200 -c 32 -p long_payload.json -T application/json https://staging-redwood/v1/generate` (long_payload has ~1500 tokens)
2) Observe `batcher_pending` climb, then `request_queue_wait > 30s`
3) See 504s from nginx after proxy_read_timeout (60s)

jess: mitigation actions taken:
- Rolled max_pending down to 48 (partial relief)
- Re-enabled early_reject threshold=30s
- Temporarily disabled continuous batching for pool A for 10m (`continuous_batching.enabled=false`)
- Rerouted Acme to fallback-model for 15m

maya: follow-up recommendations:
- Add automatic traffic shed when queue depth > 75% (reject fast with clear 429/early_reject payload)
- Make continuous-batcher aware of long-seq inflight ratio; if > 20% long-seq, prefer smaller batch windows
- Add per-tenant max_concurrent_long_requests and admission control

devon: opened issue infra#8421 with logs and synthetic repro script attached. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/issues/8421

alex: customer communication: we sent interim note at 09:10 UTC explaining it's an infrastructure admission/backlog issue, actions taken, and ETA for postmortem. Customer asked for logs for their tenant — we provided request ids and timelines.

jess: post-incident items I captured:
- Runbook: add a quick rollback knob for continuous_batching.max_pending and a one-click disable in Console.
- Dashboard: new chart `batcher_dequeue_tail` and tenant-scoped queue depth alerts.
- SLO tweak: enforce proxy_read_timeout align with gateway timeout to avoid nginx 502/504 confusion.

ops-bot: infra-alert: `pool-A-batcher-oom` flapped but no OOM observed; false positive from metric collector.

maya: final status at 09:32: traffic stable, p95 latency back to normal for most tenants, Acme confirmed reduced errors. We'll keep monitoring for 24h and prepare a write-up.

devon: note for eng-runtime: consider per-queue admission token that accounts for kv-cache warmup; currently cold KV leads to longer per-request execution which blocks batches.

alex: assigning owners: devon -> repro script + perf test, jess -> customer follow-up/postmortem write, maya -> console alert rules, infra -> implement early_reject auto-shed. I'll draft the postmortem.

jess: quick snippet we used for early_reject response body for customers: ```json
{"error":"early_reject","reason":"service-overloaded","suggestion":"retry with backoff or use smaller inputs"}
```

maya: thanks all. Closing thread once postmortem published. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: note: saved incident log to /incidents/2365004321/ and attached perf graphs.
